title: Christmas Markets With Kids: UK and Europe Family Guide
description: Christmas markets with kids: when markets open, rides, skating and Santa, tips for buggies and crowds, and European markets worth a trip.
intro: Twinkling stalls, hot chocolate and a carousel. Christmas markets are magical for kids if you time it right. Here’s how to enjoy them without the crowd crush.

image.alt: A family gathered around a Christmas tree

cardText: Timing, rides and skating, buggies and the best trips abroad.

blocks.title: Scout’s market tip
blocks.text: Go on a weekday afternoon, just as the lights come on. You get the sparkle without the evening crowds.
points: Carriers beat buggies in busy aisles
Set a budget for treats and rides
Many markets are free to enter

sections.html: Many UK markets open from mid to late November and run until just before Christmas. Weekends and evenings are busiest, so weekday afternoons are the sweet spot with children.

• Carousels and small fairground rides.
  • Pop-up ice rinks. See ice skating with kids.
  • Santa’s grottos (often bookable in advance).
  • Treats: hot chocolate, waffles and roasted chestnuts.

Europe’s famous markets in Germany, Austria and France make a magical short break. Our sister site has a guide to Christmas market city breaks, and Disneyland Paris and Tivoli Gardens both run Christmas seasons.

faqs.q: When do Christmas markets open in the UK?
faqs.a: Many open from mid to late November and close just before Christmas, but dates vary. Check the market’s own website.
